answer: A social problem I care deeply about is the lack of quality education available to children from poorer backgrounds. In my country, a child's future is too often determined by the wealth of their family, which I find genuinely [[unjust]]. Wealthier families can pay for private tutors and good schools, while poorer children often sit in overcrowded classrooms with too few teachers. This matters to me because I believe education is the most powerful tool for breaking the cycle of poverty. I also see it every day in my work, where the students who reach us are usually the lucky ones who had support from the start. It affects millions of talented children who never get the chance to [[fulfil their potential]] simply due to their circumstances. Near my hometown, for example, there are children living on the char lands, the river islands of the Jamuna, who have to cross the river by boat just to reach school, and many simply drop out. I think this is a tragic waste of human potential. To address it, I believe there needs to be far greater investment in public schools and more scholarship opportunities for the [[disadvantaged]]. Better pay for rural teachers would also help attract talented people. Honestly, I think providing equal access to good education is one of the most important things any society can do. It is an issue I feel strongly about, and I try to support relevant charities where I can. I genuinely believe that giving every child a fair start would create a more [[equitable]] and prosperous society for everyone.

followUps.q: Have you ever volunteered to help with this problem?
followUps.answer: A little. During university, I taught basic English to children in my grandparents' village during the holidays. It was only a few weeks, but seeing their enthusiasm was incredibly [[rewarding]].

followUps.q: Do you think the situation is improving?
followUps.answer: Slowly, yes. More girls are in school now than a generation ago, and mobile phones give some access to online lessons. But the gap in quality between rich and poor areas is still very wide.
